post.description: Charges a payment instrument for all or part of the remaining balance. The invoice balance does not move until the processor reports a capture, which this endpoint waits briefly for so the response's `amountPaid` and `status` usually reflect the settled state; if capture hasn't landed by the time the wait elapses, the allocation is still `pending` and the response reflects the pre-charge state. Idempotent by idempotency key per invoice — a replay returns the existing allocation without charging again.

post.description: Records money the merchant collected directly — cash, check, Zelle, and similar. There is no processor to wait on, so the allocation is applied and the invoice balance moves in the same request: a partial amount leaves the invoice `partially_paid`, and the full remaining balance marks it `paid`. Note that `effectiveAt` drives the invoice `paidAt`, so back-dating a cash payment back-dates the paid date. The recording actor is taken from the authenticated principal and is never accepted in the body. Idempotent by idempotency key per invoice.

title.description: Which metric this data point represents. `total_volume`, `transaction_count`, and `average_transaction_amount` are derived from captured payments in the window. `approval_rate` is approved authorizations divided by total resolved authorization attempts (declined + approved) in the window; attempts still pending are excluded.

amount.description: The metric value. For `total_volume` and `average_transaction_amount`, this is a currency amount in minor units (see `currency`). For `transaction_count`, this is a raw integer count. For `approval_rate`, this is a unitless ratio from 0 to 1 (not a percentage) — e.g. 0.9 means a 90% approval rate.

currency.description: ISO currency code for money metrics, null for transaction_count (no currency) and approval_rate (unitless ratio).

trend.description: Normalized change ratio from -1 to 1 for the selected window versus the previous window. Unitless ratio (not percent): 1 = +100% change, 0.5 = +50%, 0 = no change, -0.25 = -25%, -1 = -100%. For approval_rate, this is the change in the ratio itself (current rate minus previous rate, normalized), not a change in percentage points.
